categories.name: Overall aesthetic
categories.summary: Dark found-footage iceberg documentary. Seven levels, calm narrator, VHS/CRT texture, tiny mono type, cyan ice titles.

rules.text: Build every video as an iceberg with exactly 7 levels. Put about 3-4 entries in each level (19-32 in total). Make later levels longer and darker. 14 of 14 refs.
rules.title: Iceberg format, 7 levels

rules.text: Aim for 45-65 min. The refs run 42.6-87.5 min; 12 of 14 are 43-67 min.
rules.title: Length

rules.text: Fill 60-80 % of the runtime with real found footage: CCTV, dashcam, phone, livestream, news, bodycam. Use screenshots and stills for the rest (est.).
rules.title: Found footage first

rules.text: Put a heavy vignette, grain and light still CRT texture over footage, never so dark that details are lost. No moving static/noise overlay except on the warning card. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rules.title: VHS/CRT texture

rules.text: Cut to the host in a red-lit room with an evidence board every 3-6 min, at seams. Keep the host to about 4-10 % of runtime. 13 of 14 refs (not 2TAT).
rules.title: Host cutaways

rules.text: Use the same card set in every video: warning card, animated iceberg list, ONE case title card (slow gentle shake + eased zoom + textured reveal), typed date, name tag, source credit, animated maps. No Presents sting, no headline/web graphics. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rules.title: Same kit every video

rules.text: Censor gore, bodies, faces of victims and minors. Add the small 'VISUALS ALTERED FOR VISUAL SAFETY' note on altered shots.
rules.title: Respect and safety

rules.text: No sponsor reads. The only plugs are subscribe (mid) and Patreon 'level eight' (end).
rules.title: No on-screen sponsor

categories.name: Mood and emotion
categories.summary: Cold, uneasy, slow dread that grows level by level. Never jokey.

rules.text: Start mild at Level 1. Grow darker each level. Say it in the hook: 'begin with the mildly chilling and with each level descend into the truly horrifying'.
rules.title: Descend into dread

rules.text: Show the normal moment first. Then turn: 'However,' or 'what happened next was ...'. The dread comes from the calm before the turn.
rules.title: Ordinary then wrong

rules.text: Keep tone neutral and factual. No shouting, no meme cuts, no jokes.
rules.title: Calm, not hype

rules.text: Use rare 2-3 frame glitch/RGB-split cuts when something feels wrong or a level changes; no static-noise overlay on footage. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rules.title: Uncanny glitches

rules.text: When the case has no answer, end the entry on the open question ('remains unsolved', 'to this day'). Do not explain it away.
rules.title: Leave it open

rules.text: Treat deaths with care. Censor, do not linger on gore, and state outcomes plainly.
rules.title: Respect the victims

categories.name: Color palette
categories.summary: Near-monochrome dark footage. Accents: cyan ice, red alerts, yellow highlight, orange tags.

rules.text: Keep footage muted. Measured saturation median is 3.1-10.8 (signalstats SATAVG). Desaturate bright clips toward that.
rules.title: Low saturation

rules.text: Keep average luma dark-mid. Measured YAVG median is 52-73 out of 255.
rules.title: Dark mid luma

rules.text: Crush the blacks. Let edges fall to black under the vignette.
rules.title: Crushed blacks

rules.text: Tint single clips teal, red, sepia or yellow to mark mood or a flashback. One tint per clip.
rules.title: Per-clip tints

rules.text: Sensitive or stock footage keeps the normal dark Abyssal grade; cover faces with mosaic/blur. No inverted, mirrored or posterised colour looks on clips at all, intro included; clips keep only the normal Abyssal grade. (owner 2026-11-12, storyboard v6)
rules.title: Normal grade on sensitive clips

rules.text: Use glowing cyan/white only for iceberg level and entry titles.
rules.title: Cyan for ice titles

rules.text: Use red for the date cursor block, money/stat numbers, censored words, arrows and circles.
rules.title: Red for danger

rules.text: Use yellow highlighter on the key phrase in an article. Use yellow for the second speaker in captions.
rules.title: Yellow for the key line

rules.text: Use an orange (or red) box with dark mono text for name tags in case videos.
rules.title: Orange or red name box

rules.text: Grade: do not darken clips. No 0.92 dim, light vignette only (about 15 %). NO grain or noise layer on clips or cards: a fixed grain over a moving/pushing picture reads as moving static lines. Keep the v6 colour balance (owner 2026-11-13: 'rest colorgrade was good').
rules.title: Bright grade, no grain

categories.name: Lighting
categories.summary: Footage is used as found. Graphics glow out of darkness.

rules.text: Do not relight or brighten found footage much. Keep night CCTV and dashcam dark.
rules.title: Keep found light

rules.text: Light the host room red and low, with the evidence board behind.
rules.title: Red host room

rules.text: Give ice titles and Level cards a soft glow and bloom out of the dark background.
rules.title: Glow on titles

rules.text: Use a strong vignette on every shot to pull the eye to the centre.
rules.title: Vignette

categories.name: Camera angles
categories.summary: Angles come from the source: CCTV high angle, dashcam forward, phone POV.

rules.text: Keep the real CCTV/dashcam/phone frame. Do not crop out timestamps or the camera's own overlay unless they reveal private data.
rules.title: Show the source angle

rules.text: Centre vertical phone clips on a blurred or dark copy of the clip. Or show 2-3 as narrow side-by-side strips.
rules.title: Vertical clips

rules.text: Frame the host in a static medium shot, chest up, evidence board behind.
rules.title: Host medium shot

rules.text: Do not build article, web or headline screenshot graphics. (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rules.title: Stills full frame

categories.name: Camera movement
categories.summary: Little real movement. Slow digital zooms on stills; shake comes from the source.

rules.text: Hold photos still (no Ken Burns). Make them move with typed text, a highlight wipe, a red circle, a colour change or a 3-5 degree tilt. Only the iceberg list (slow eased zoom-in), the case title card (very slow gentle shake + small zoom) and maps move the camera. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rules.title: Still stills

rules.text: Do not scroll the iceberg list; hold it 3.4-3.6 s with the text frozen in place (only the iceberg backdrop may drift slightly) and glitch out. A long page may scroll only if the inset photo must grow with it.
rules.title: No list scroll

rules.text: Zoom in on the key person or object in CCTV, then add a red arrow, circle or spotlight.
rules.title: Punch-in on the detail

rules.text: Never add camera shake to footage clips. The only added shake is the very slow gentle shake on the case title card. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rules.title: No fake shake

rules.text: Keep the host camera locked.
rules.title: Static host

rules.text: Freeze or cut away just before the worst moment. Censor what follows.
rules.title: Freeze before impact

categories.name: Shot composition
categories.summary: Centred, dark-edged frames. Tiny mono text in fixed corners.

rules.text: Put the date top-left (or big in the centre), the source credit bottom-left, the safety note bottom-right, the captions bottom-centre.
rules.title: Fixed corners

rules.text: Centre Level cards and ice entry titles.
rules.title: Centred titles

rules.text: Fill unused frame around vertical clips and small photos with a blurred copy of the same image.
rules.title: Blur fill

rules.text: Show a person's photo as a small inset over a blurred copy of itself, or as white-bordered stills side by side with tiny caps names below.
rules.title: Photo inset

rules.text: Use vertical split panels to compare two or three clips or people.
rules.title: Split screen

rules.text: Place mosaic blocks tight on faces, bodies and plates. Use black boxes on names in screenshots.
rules.title: Censor in frame

rules.text: Show old-internet pages inside a glowing CRT or old-Mac window.
rules.title: CRT window for old web

categories.name: Editing rhythm
categories.summary: Hard cuts, about 6-7 per min in the body; the intro is much faster.

rules.text: Average shot length is 5.0-7.6 s (median ~6.0 s, about 10 cuts/min) in all 14 refs, measured with glitch bursts merged. Shots without glitches average 5.5-7.7 s.
rules.title: Body pace

rules.text: Hold most shots about 3-8 s; never under 3 s, no exceptions. Hold the first case of a video longer. (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rules.title: Real shot length

rules.text: Cut the first 2 min fastest: about 30-50 cuts in the first 120 s (median about 38).
rules.title: Fast intro

rules.text: Land 'Level 1' at 24-47 s. Do not let the intro run long.
rules.title: Level 1 early

rules.text: Build the teaser just before the first case from real raw case clips, each >= 3 s (no 1-2 s shock clips). (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rules.title: Teaser montage

rules.text: CCTV and dashcam incident runs also keep every shot >= 3 s (no fast-cut exception). (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rules.title: Fast CCTV

rules.text: No article-screenshot holds (no web/headline graphics); show real footage instead. (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rules.title: Hold screenshots

rules.text: At each level change: about 1 s black, 0.7-1 s silence, then the Level card.
rules.title: Level seam

rules.text: Space the levels so Level 2 starts at about 4-6 min, Level 4 at about 15-19 min, and Level 7 in the last 15-20 min.
rules.title: Level timing

rules.text: Make each entry about 2 min: median 126 s (middle half 102-152 s, n=335), about 21 shots per entry. Deeper levels run longer: Level 1 ~109 s, Levels 6-7 ~135 s.
rules.title: Entry length

rules.text: Use 16-32 entries per video (median ~22; one 87-min ref has 50). Videos run 43-67 min with 374-693 shots.
rules.title: Entry count

rules.text: Use glitch cuts often but short: 3-89 per video (median ~42), each 0.2-0.3 s, about 0.7% of screen time.
rules.title: Glitch count

categories.name: Transitions
categories.summary: Hard cuts by default. Black dips at seams. Glitch bursts for shocks.

rules.text: Use hard cuts for nearly every edit.
rules.title: Hard cuts

rules.text: Dip to black for about 1 s before each Level card.
rules.title: Black dip at levels

rules.text: Scramble the ice entry title in over 3-4 frames after 0.1-2.0 s of black, hold 1.5-3.5 s, then glitch it out in 2 frames. Set it as white wide caps with a few cyan-tinted letters and a soft glow, centred at about 43-50% height, one or two lines, 25-50% of frame width, over a slowly pushing-in iceberg.
rules.title: Ice title motion

rules.text: Use a 2-3 frame glitch cut only for shock cuts; no static-noise bursts over footage (static lives on the warning card only). (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rules.title: Glitch sting

rules.text: Start with 0.7-3.0 s of black, then fade the Level card in over 3 frames from 20-40% brightness. Set the text at ~42% of frame width, centred at y 50%, over the iceberg picture. Push it to ~80% width over 1.2-2.5 s, then zoom through in 3 frames into the iceberg close-up and the first ice title.
rules.title: Level card motion

rules.text: Between calm stills or state/place cards use a dip to black, never a dissolve. (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rules.title: Soft dissolve rarely

rules.text: Shock moments use a dip, a red circle or a short dark glitch cut, never a posterised/inverted flash. No inverted, mirrored or posterised colour looks on clips at all, intro included; clips keep only the normal Abyssal grade. (owner 2026-11-12, storyboard v6)
rules.title: No posterise flash

rules.text: Use no spins or light leaks. Allowed exceptions: the 3-frame zoom-through from the Level card into the first ice title, and the raven/silhouette wipe onto the Patreon card.
rules.title: Only two wipes

categories.name: Typography
categories.summary: Tiny monospace typewriter type everywhere; big white slab for 'Level N'; glowing caps for ice titles.

rules.text: Set dates, tags, credits, captions and list rows in a monospace typewriter font, caps.
rules.title: Mono base

rules.text: Keep most text small. Only 'Level N' and big centre dates are large.
rules.title: Small

rules.text: Set 'Level N' in big white bold mono/slab.
rules.title: Level card type

rules.text: Set entry titles in wide-tracked glowing cyan/white caps, 1-2 lines, centred.
rules.title: Ice title type

rules.text: Type dates and captions on letter by letter or word by word.
rules.title: Typed-on

rules.text: End a typed date with a red block cursor on the last character.
rules.title: Red cursor

rules.text: Captions for found audio: white for speaker 1, yellow for the reply. Bracket sounds: '[screaming]'.
rules.title: Caption colours

rules.text: Show censored words in red mono with asterisks ('M*rd*rs'), even in titles.
rules.title: Censored words

rules.text: Wipe every highlight band left to right, never pop it: about 3 words/s (one line in 1-3 s), starting 0.4-1.5 s after the cut. Yellow/amber for key text, red for danger words. Draw the band as an amber marker with a thin dark lower edge, text left readable on top. Alternative: a yellow double-arrow underline (about 35% frame wide) that steps down one line every ~2 s, matched to the spoken words.
rules.title: Highlights wipe

rules.text: Type dates, credits and quotes at 1-1.5 characters per frame at 10 fps. Swap caption lines hard, about 1.8 s each.
rules.title: Typing speed

rules.text: Iceberg (case list) card: no highlight on any case name (all the same white). Static CRT look on it: fixed scanlines, soft glow, small red/blue edge, curved screen with dark rounded corners. No noise, rolling bar or flicker. Slow eased zoom, no shake.
rules.title: Iceberg: no highlight, CRT

rules.text: The iceberg card gets a strong smooth vignette on top of the CRT look. The centre stays clean. The edges go about 55 % darker.
rules.title: Iceberg: CRT plus vignette

categories.name: Music and sound
categories.summary: Quiet master, low drone bed, raw clip audio on key moments, true silence at seams.

rules.text: Master around -21 to -25 LUFS integrated. Refs measure -20.2 to -27.6 LUFS (median about -22.5).
rules.title: Quiet master

rules.text: Make the first 90 s about 2-5 LU louder than the body (refs: intro -18.5 to -22.8 LUFS).
rules.title: Louder intro

rules.text: Run a low, dark ambient drone or music bed under all narration. Keep it well under the voice.
rules.title: Drone bed

rules.text: Drop the narration and let raw clip audio play in the hook and at the key moment of each incident.
rules.title: Raw audio on key clips

rules.text: Leave about 1 s of true silence at each level change and 1-3 s at the very end.
rules.title: Silence at seams

rules.text: Bleep swearing in raw audio.
rules.title: Bleep swears

rules.text: Put a high-band static tick (+24 to +35 dB above the bed, measured) on every glitch cut. Put a low boom (+17 to +24 dB) on full date cards, red numbers and the Patreon wipe. Put a high riser (+17 to +30 dB) into highlight wipes, arrows and spotlights. Leave captions, credits, safety notes, circles, splits and black boxes silent.
rules.title: Sound on events

rules.text: Keep the loudness range moderate (refs 3.5-9.3 LU). No loud jump scares.
rules.title: Low LRA

rules.text: Keep the narrator clear and steady above the bed at all times.
rules.title: Narration on top

categories.name: Storytelling
categories.summary: Fixed iceberg script: hook, 7 levels, calm date-first case stories, Patreon level eight.

rules.text: Open with: warning card (2-3 s), raw-audio hook with captions over raw footage, animated iceberg/list graphic for the N-cases line (4-5 s), teaser of raw clips (>= 3 s each), then the first case title card. No Presents sting. (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rules.title: Open

rules.text: Say the count and the frame: 'N <things>, seven levels... let's start at the tip of the iceberg'.
rules.title: Hook line

rules.text: Optional: one first-person line of effort ('I've personally searched through countless videos...').
rules.title: Host claim

rules.text: Each entry: 'Level N' + spoken title, ice title card, typed date, name tag, then the story.
rules.title: Entry order

rules.text: Start each story with the date and place ('On June 30, 2014, in ...').
rules.title: Date first

rules.text: Date/place/person -> ordinary moment ('had no idea') -> 'However,' -> incident -> investigation -> legal outcome or open question.
rules.title: Story arc

rules.text: Write short, past-tense, third-person sentences. Use exact numbers and facts.
rules.title: Short past tense

rules.text: Before Level 4, add one short subscribe line ('subscribe and stay with us').
rules.title: Mid CTA

rules.text: For mysteries add theories and a question hook ('Mystery solved? ...'), then leave it open.
rules.title: Mystery entries

rules.text: End with: 'tip of the iceberg' line, next-iceberg teaser, Patreon 'level eight' plug ('link in the description'), black card 'THANKS FOR WATCHING'.
rules.title: Outro

rules.text: For dark mystery topics you may stop on the last unresolved fact with no recap (3 of 14 refs).
rules.title: Or stop cold

rules.text: Open each entry on its ice title card (210 of 335 entries). Otherwise open on stock, archive footage or a photo, with the title said in voice-over.
rules.title: Entry opener

rules.text: Fill screen time mostly with real footage: archive/documentary ~29%, stock ~18%, photos ~10%, host ~7% (0-14%; 5 of 14 refs have no host), CCTV ~5%, dashcam ~4%, phone ~3%. Cards and titles are under 5% in total.
rules.title: Shot mix

rulebook.text: Every video is an iceberg with exactly 7 levels. Each level opens with a black dip, about 1 s silence and the 'Level N' card.
rulebook.title: Seven levels

rulebook.text: Open in this order: warning card (2-3 s), raw-audio hook with mono captions over real raw footage, the 'N cases' animated iceberg list (7 s), teaser of intense-movement raw clips (each >= 3 s), first case by about 45 s. The intro is mostly real raw clips, not graphics. No Presents sting. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Fixed opening

rulebook.text: Every entry gets: glowing ice title, typed date with red cursor, name tag, source credit. No entry without a date.
rulebook.title: Entry card set

rulebook.text: All small text is monospace typewriter caps. 'Level N' is big white bold mono. Ice titles are glowing wide caps. No other fonts.
rulebook.title: Mono type only

rulebook.text: Keep the dark, low-saturation look (vignette, grain, light tape texture) but never too dark: details inside the image must stay clearly visible; lift shadows rather than crush them. Colour only in tints, red alerts and circles, yellow highlights and cyan ice. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Dark but readable

rulebook.text: Mosaic faces, bodies and plates; black-box names; bleep swears; red asterisk words; blur every TV channel / media-group logo in footage; add 'VISUALS ALTERED FOR VISUAL SAFETY'. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Censor everything sensitive

rulebook.text: Narration is calm, flat, third person, past tense, and starts each story with the date.
rulebook.title: Calm date-first narration

rulebook.text: Transitions: hard cuts by default, dips to black between beats, a few short crossfades allowed (see crossfade rule). Glitch cuts (2-3 frames, no overlap) only rarely: intro and shock moments. (owner 2026-11-13, v6 render; replaces v4 hard-cuts-only)
rulebook.title: Hard cuts and dips only

rulebook.text: Master about -21 to -25 LUFS, intro 2-5 LU louder. A dark horror ambience bed runs under the voice, with good SFX on events, both from Epidemic Sound; raw audio on key clips. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Quiet mix

rulebook.text: End with the 'level eight on Patreon' plug and the black 'THANKS FOR WATCHING' card (unless the topic ends cold).
rulebook.title: Patreon level eight

rulebook.text: Graphics move only by typing, left-to-right highlight wipes, red circles drawing on, rare 2-3 frame glitch cuts, dips through black, animated maps (MAP_SPEC) and two ref camera moves: the iceberg list (slow eased zoom-in, no shake) and the case title card (very slow gentle shake + small eased zoom-in). Never camera shake on footage clips. Sound sits on those events. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Few kinds of motion

rulebook.text: Narration: whole sentences, always. Cut AI fillers (yeah/ya/ia) out between words at the quietest point, never mute them into a silent hole. Pauses only at sentence ends (~0.4 s) and commas (~0.2 s), never mid-sentence. Every pause >= 0.15 s is true silence (80 ms word tail, 50 ms ramp in): AI voices leave low noise/garble there that reads as a leak. Never cut into the first word of a take: check where it really starts. Preview with a fixed gain, not loudnorm (it lifts the leaks). Verify: Whisper hears all script words, no fillers. Tool: productions/abyssal-01-theme-park-disasters/build/vo_v7.py. (owner 2026-11-13)
rulebook.title: Clean audio cuts

rulebook.text: The warning card sits on one steady, continuous, normal-pitched VHS/TV static bed (low-pass the harsh highs). No repeated bursts, pops or pitch jumps: it never disrupts the viewer's flow. Level per the refs (about -15 LUFS over the warning) unless it feels harsh; then lower it. (owner 2026-11-12, v2; Presents removed v3)
rulebook.title: Steady intro static

rulebook.text: Before building, study the reference intros frame by frame (warning, hook, N-cases list, title presentation, case card, date, name tag, glitch, safety note): their motion, easing and flow. Copy them as closely as possible; the intro motion graphics must match the refs (owner 2026-11-12, v2 did not). Owner overrides (warning length, no Presents, one case card) win over the refs.
rulebook.title: Match the refs by eye

rulebook.text: Every victim face in every frame is fully covered: mosaic box larger than the whole face and hair edge, tracked through motion, on every photo of an article card too. QC every victim shot frame by frame (every ~0.5 s).
rulebook.title: Faces fully covered

rulebook.text: Glitch and static hits sit under the narration: 30 ms peak at most about the voice's p90 level (refs: 0 to +3 dB over voice p90, short-term at voice level). No hit jumps out. Only the intro static bed is louder.
rulebook.title: Quiet glitch hits

rulebook.text: Moving static/noise lives only on the warning card. No constant moving static, noise bands, tracking lines or VHS-noise overlay on footage; footage keeps only a light, still tape look (soft chroma bleed, faint scanlines, grain). Overrides the old 'VHS over everything'. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Static only on the warning card

rulebook.text: Crossfades (6-12 f) are allowed in a few places: between calm shots inside a story beat or out of a map/graphic. Hard cuts stay the default; dips to black between beats. Never on the exact word cut, never with a glitch. (owner 2026-11-13, v6 render; overrides the v4 no-crossfade rule)
rulebook.title: No overlapping frames

rulebook.text: Glitch frames and censored shots stay dark and low saturation (SATAVG ~3-11, YAVG ~52-73). No colourful posterise; a full mosaic plus dark grade covers sensitive frames.
rulebook.title: Dark low-saturation glitch

rulebook.text: Follow styleguide/_shared/GENERIC_RULES.md (shot length >= 3 s, audio cutting, SFX/music levels, loudness, transition hygiene, smoothness, QC, feedback loop). This guide's own rule book wins only where it says so explicitly.
rulebook.title: Generic rules

rulebook.text: Every owner note on a render goes into this guide the same day (rule book entry or rule, plus a Learnings entry, via model.apply_ops + model.save). The next build must read the rule book, the open Learnings and styleguide/_shared/GENERIC_RULES.md first; after each render check it against every line, fix what fails, then deliver.
rulebook.title: Feedback loop

rulebook.text: Picture matches the narration word by word: one clip per sentence, the sentence covers its clip (cut on the sentence/clause start, the clip ends with the sentence), so the place, ride, person or thing appears when it is said. Every clip >= 3 s: merge short sentences rather than make short clips. Real footage; no generic filler; no website/headline graphics. Plan it per sentence in the storyboard from the final narration timings. (owner 2026-11-12 v5, 2026-11-13 v6 render)
rulebook.title: Picture follows narration

rulebook.text: The warning card holds 2-3 s in total (60-90 f at 30 fps), then hard-cuts or dips to black into the hook. Overrides the old 4-5 s rule and the 208 f ref measurement. (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rulebook.title: Short warning card

rulebook.text: Never show 'PRESENTS' or 'ABYSSAL DETECTIVE PRESENTS' anywhere: there is no name to present. The warning card goes straight into the raw-audio hook. (owner 2026-11-12, v3)
rulebook.title: No Presents text

rulebook.text: The 'N cases/disasters' line gets the animated iceberg list held 7 s: every case name sharp and readable (no blur or pixelation on deeper entries), a clear slow eased zoom-in running the whole time the names show (no shake), light grain texture. No headline or website screenshots. Spec: productions/_abyssal-ref/INTRO_SPEC3.md. (owner 2026-11-12 v5, zoom stressed 2026-11-13)
rulebook.title: Iceberg graphic for the N-cases line

rulebook.text: Each case gets ONE title card: iceberg plate with a very slow gentle camera shake and a small eased zoom-in, textured text 'CASE 01' with the case name below it. No second card, no ice close-up swap. Music plays under the title card. Then the case footage starts (hard cut or dip to black, no crossfade); the date is small text on the first footage shot. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Case title card like the refs

rulebook.text: Before any render, build the storyboard as a private web page, show it to the owner and get approval. No render without an approved storyboard. (owner 2026-11-12, v3)
rulebook.title: Storyboard approval first

rulebook.text: Every clip is on screen at least 3 s (90 f at 30 fps), the warning card excepted (2-3 s). No montage, teaser, shock-burst or CCTV/dashcam exception. (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rulebook.title: Every clip at least 3 s

rulebook.text: No website, article or headline screenshot motion graphics anywhere. Show the story with real footage, photos and the ref card set instead. (owner 2026-11-12, v4)
rulebook.title: No web or headline graphics

rulebook.text: Fill the intro with real raw footage with intense movement (news, phone, CCTV, archive of the actual cases), not graphics. Graphics in the intro are only the warning card and the iceberg list. No inverted, mirrored or posterised colour looks on clips at all, intro included; clips keep only the normal Abyssal grade. (owner 2026-11-12, storyboard v6)
rulebook.title: Raw clips in the intro

rulebook.text: Use free footage only. News and raw case footage is OK with an on-screen source credit. Never licensed, paid or watermarked stock. Fill gaps with Pexels or Pixabay clips. More motion graphics are welcome (maps, red circles, typed text). (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Free clips only

rulebook.text: Show places with proper animated maps built to productions/_abyssal-ref/MAP_SPEC.md (dark map, eased country-to-town push, glowing pin, typed label, drawn route line), or write the place name centred on screen, or use a drone/establishing shot with the name. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Animated maps for places

rulebook.text: Mark things with a red circle or strong red highlight drawn on. Never white X marks. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: Red circles, not X marks

rulebook.text: No 1-3 frame flash of another shot at any cut (check every cut frame by frame). Every graphic (documents, text cards, maps) is centred on the frame, never right of centre. (owner 2026-11-12, v5)
rulebook.title: No frame leaks, centred graphics

rulebook.text: Vary the motion graphics inside one video: name tags, date stamps, place names, highlights/red circles and document callouts must not all use the same design and animation every time. Repeating a design across different videos is fine; within one video it must not feel repetitive. Study the refs for more MG types and when to use each. (owner 2026-11-12, storyboard v6)
rulebook.title: Vary the motion graphics

rulebook.text: New source span: before use, look at its first, middle and last frames. No news headline, caption, logo swirl or dissolve may show. If one shows, move the source in point past it (v7 r31 and r39).

Red circle on a moving person: check the tracked circle in a frame strip. If it slides off the person, place it by hand from keyframes read off the frames (v7 r31: tracker locked onto the slide pattern).

SFX level: never place SFX relative to the voice. Follow GENERIC C20-22: music ~13 dB under the VO, SFX under the music, SFX inside narration peak ~-30 dBFS and 6-8 dB under the VO. Booms/risers only on transitions or gaps (v7 SFX were too loud, owner 2026-11-13).
Intro: warning card leaves with a short glitch transition (6-8 f) plus a quiet low-passed glitch SFX.
Intro: on the case count line ('twenty-five of them') zoom-in transition to the iceberg, zoomed in so every case name reads, list slides up 3-4 s, then dip to black.
Intro: the narration is fast. Change the clip with each topic (one clip per idea), even inside a long sentence.
Intro: raw crowd screams under the ride clips, like the clip's own audio, quiet (about 18 dB under the VO).
Intro montage for list lines (gate / ticket office / ride check): dark grey panel; each card slides up to centre and fades in; the old card slides up and fades out.
Intro end: iceberg again, scroll to the top with a dip to black, highlight case 01 on its name, dip to black into the title card.

Card-slide montage: each clip has a red border; keep a clear gap between the leaving card and the arriving card. Background is black with a grey radial gradient (soft white highlight in the centre) and a vignette, for a horror feel; not a flat grey panel.
Audio: every audio cut is a crossfade (raw clip audio, music bed joins, SFX tails). Nothing starts or stops abruptly.
Music plays under the whole video, from the first frame to the last, with no gaps; beds join by crossfades.
Level ladder (owner 2026-11-13): narration 100 %, music 80 %, SFX 60 %. Narration is always on top, music under it, SFX under the music.

Card montage exit: the last red-border card morphs out: its border spreads to the frame edges while the clip zooms to full screen, then it crossfades into the next shot (iceberg zoomed onto case 01 with the highlight).
Mix level ladder, owner pick A: voice on top; music ~10 dB under the voice; SFX ~14 dB under the voice (replaces the 13 dB music rule for Abyssal).
Map animations play their full real length, retimed evenly to the clip slot. Never read a map past its real end (no padded last frame, no freeze).

Motion graphics move slowly with strong easing (smootherstep or ease-in-out quint). Entrances, exits, slides, zooms, morphs and wipes last at least 0.6-1.0 s (18-30 f). Typing at about 0.5-0.7 characters per frame. Nothing reads as fast forward.
Start of the video: the whole mix fades in over 1.5 s. Never start the audio at full level.
Every transition is 0.5 s (15 f). Crossfades 15 f, eased. Dip to black 15 f in all (8 f down, 7 f up, eased). Never 3-frame dips.
No leaked frames: a clip (and its crossfade tail) must end before any cut in its source. Scan every played source span, tail included, before the render; after the render run a leak scan.
Narration never gets a fade-in. Fade-ins go on raw clips only. Level the narration so quiet words do not sound like a fade-in.
Use a few more crossfades between shots (where the next shot has no graphic in its first 15 f).
Title and chapter music starts on the black frame of the dip to black, with a 2 s fade-in.
Every highlight graphic (red ring, document band or underline, iceberg highlight) gets a smooth eased push-in zoom on the highlighted part, so the viewer can read it.

graphics.title: Warning card
graphics.text: Black VHS-noise frame. Bands of white dash-noise and grey horizontal smear scroll over the top and bottom edges. Grey-white pixel caps, no box: 'WARNING:' (~25% width, centred, y 44%) blurs in at +0.2 s, 'FLASH IMAGE SHOWN' (~58% width, y 56%) at +0.5 s. Text garbles for 1-2 frames at irregular moments. Hold 4-5 s in total (owner 2026-11-12 overrides the refs' 6.9 s), hard cut out into the raw-audio hook. No Presents text after it. Sound: no hit at the cut; a small high-band tick (+10 to +25 dB) as the text appears. Variant: 'VIEWERS DISCRETION IS ADVISED' + red WARNING over a small iceberg, 0.6 s blown static, 2 black frames, red 'FLASH WARNING' skull.
graphics.avoid: Do not make it big or colourful.

graphics.title: Discretion logo
graphics.text: Pixel iceberg logo with 'VIEWERS DISCRETION IS ADVISED', 0-2 s.
graphics.avoid: Do not hold it longer than 2 s.

graphics.title: Iceberg entry list
graphics.text: Full-frame iceberg (sky above, dark water below), light teal fog, white waterline at about 28% down. Small white Courier rows about 3-4% of frame tall and 12-25% wide, in two loose columns (left column centred near x 40%, right near x 65%), stepping down the iceberg in about 12 rows. Owner v5: every row sharp white and readable (no blur/pixelation on deeper rows); slow eased zoom-in, no shake, hold 7 s. One variant adds thick white bars (about 1% tall) between 6 bands of rows while the iceberg is still dark. In: hard cut. Hold 3.4-3.6 s, static (no scroll seen in 6 strips), slight text shimmer. Out: 2-3 frame RGB/scanline tear, then hard cut. Sound: no fixed rule (hit 2, drop 1, none 3 of 6).
graphics.use: Before Level 1, to show what is coming.
graphics.avoid: Do not blur or pixelate deep rows; do not shake it.

graphics.title: Level card
graphics.text: Iceberg picture (cloudy sky, waterline at ~32% height, dark teal submerged ice, black sea), bold off-white slab-serif typewriter 'Level N' centred at y 50-55%, about 41% of frame width at the start of the hold, no box, no glow. In: 0.7-3.0 s of quiet black, then a 3-frame fade-in (text starts at 20-40% brightness). Hold 1.2-2.5 s with a slow push-in: the text grows from ~42% to ~80% width. Out: fast 3-frame blur zoom-through into the iceberg peak close-up. The first ice title then types on over it: white sans caps with a cyan glow, ~37% wide at y 45%, with a glitchy letter scramble while typing (5 of 6; 1 glitch smear). Sound: riser ~+10 dB over 0.3 s into the out (3 of 6), then silence.
graphics.use: Start of each of the 7 levels.
graphics.avoid: Do not skip the black dip and silence. Do not add a box behind the text.

graphics.title: Ice entry title
graphics.text: Iceberg close-up (pale blue-white ice, dark teal sky and shadows). Small white letter-spaced sans caps (Montserrat/Gotham-like), 1-2 lines, 37-45% width, centred at y 42-52%, no box. The colour runs white to cyan/teal across the line (last words cyan) with a soft cyan glow. In: 0.1-1.4 s black, then a 3-4 frame character scramble/blur-in while the ice crossfades up. Hold 1.5-3.5 s, text still, ice drifts or zooms slowly. Out: 2-frame RGB glitch smear, hard cut, or back to black. Sound: no fixed rule; a riser or a glitch tick both occur.
graphics.avoid: Do not use other colours or fonts. Owner v4: no crossfades or dissolves; enter by hard cut or dip to black.

graphics.title: State/place card
graphics.text: 'STATE - TOPIC' in condensed caps over ice texture, soft dissolve, about 3 s (KTKZ).
graphics.avoid: Do not use maps instead. Owner v4: no crossfades or dissolves; enter by hard cut or dip to black.
graphics.situation: Name a place or move to a new place

graphics.title: Typed date
graphics.text: White bitmap/VHS mono caps with a thin dark edge, no box, about 10% of frame tall, at y 48-55% (middle of the frame). Short dates are centred (x 26-73%); long dates start at x 7% and run to about 94%. Red block cursor (about 3% wide) after the last character while typing. Types on at 1-1.5 characters per frame at 10 fps ('SEPTEMBER 24, 2024' in 1.2 s), from the cut or +0.1 s. Sits over the shot as it is (the shot may be a bright collage), so keep the edge dark for contrast. Hold 0.5-1.3 s with the cursor blinking, then fade out over 5-8 frames as the next shot fades up. Over footage: small top-left, 15-25% width. Sound: as a full card, a low boom at the cut (+18 to +24 dB, 4 of 6); as an overlay, silent.
graphics.avoid: Do not show a date without the type-on. Do not use a serif or smooth font.

graphics.title: Name tag (box)
graphics.text: Solid orange (or red) box with black bold Courier text in mixed case, about 38% of frame width and ~10% tall, at y 79-94% (over the bottom of the face, or directly under a centred photo card and as wide as the card). Rough ragged edge, slight dark outline or shadow. In: a thin orange line grows, then the text reveals/types, 3-4 frames, at +0.2-1.2 s into the shot. Hold 1-3 s. Out: hard cut with the shot, or a hard drop-out while the shot keeps playing. Sound: at most a small glitch/static tick.
graphics.use: First time a person appears in case videos.
graphics.avoid: Do not reuse for the same person twice.

graphics.title: Name tag (plain)
graphics.text: Text with no box and a thin shadow, two looks. (a) Typewriter name, pale pink-white, bottom centre (x 26-74%, ~48% width, y 88-92%). (b) Small bold sans caps name ('CRYSTAL SHELDON') over a thin rule and a small mixed-case role line ('Exotic Animal Trainer'), lower right of centre (x 56-84%, ~28% width, y 83-92%). In: fade/type over 3-8 frames, usually late (+1.8-3.5 s); one clip already shows it at +1 s. Hold 1.0-2.5 s to the shot end. Out: hard cut or digital glitch. Sound: small high-band tick (6 of 6).
graphics.avoid: Do not mix both tag styles in one video.

graphics.title: Source credit
graphics.text: Tiny white mono caps ('COURTESY: ...'), 8-15% width, top-right or bottom-left. Present from the cut, static for the whole shot, silent. Rarely typed on 1 character per frame. Variant seen: a dark-navy box with white bold sans caps 'NAME / OUTLET', about 32% wide and 5% tall, top-right (x 68-100%, y 7-12%), static while the picture zooms, gone at the next shot. That one may be part of the source clip.
graphics.avoid: Do not make it big.

graphics.title: Safety note
graphics.text: 'VISUALS ALTERED FOR VISUAL SAFETY' in tiny bold white caps (about 2.5% of frame tall), bottom-right at the very edge: x 66-99%, y 96-98%. 30-34% of the video area's width, no box, over the footage with a soft dark vignette behind it. Present by +0.4 s, static for the whole shot, silent. When the video is an inset, keep it at the inset's bottom-right.
graphics.use: On every censored or altered shot.
graphics.avoid: Do not leave it off censored shots. Do not move or animate it.

graphics.title: Mosaic censor
graphics.text: Square pixel blocks, cells ~3-4% of frame width, tight on faces (block ~18% wide for a child in a group photo, up to ~25-30% for a close face), bodies and plates. On a still it is present from the first frame, tracks the subject as the photo drifts, static to the end. On moving footage small blocks can start on the edges and a large block (~42% wide, ~75% tall) covers a window or body by ~3 s. Usually with the safety note. Variant: full-frame pixel ramp, 1 frame in, peak at ~0.7 s, eases to blur over ~1.5 s. Sound: low boom (+20 dB) only on heavy reveals (2 of 6); else none.
graphics.avoid: Do not use soft blur alone on gore.

graphics.title: Red censored word
graphics.text: Red bold word or phrase (asterisk censoring 'M*rd*rs'). Two looks. (a) Key phrase in red (about #E8262A) inside a white bold sans 2-line headline on a black band (~92% wide, x 4-96%, y 40-60%) with a tiny grey caps source tag above the first line; the red phrase ends the second line. (b) Bold red mono/slab caps with dark outline, lower left (x 5-63%, y 85-92%), letters scrambled for the first frames then resolving, gone by ~1.6 s. Fades in over 2-10 frames, placed 1.8-3.9 s after the cut. Sound: none.
graphics.use: Swears and violent words in text.
graphics.avoid: Do not print the word in full.

graphics.title: Raw-audio caption
graphics.text: One line of small white Courier, mixed case, lower centre, 35-45% width, thin dark outline. Hard swap per line (0 frames), ~1.8 s per line, no fade. Yellow only for the second speaker or one emphasised phrase. '[Bracketed sounds]' in the same spot (y 93-96%), Title Case ('[Continues Walking]', '[Multiple Gunshots Noises]'), 28-38% width, 1.2-2.8 s, no box, with short gaps with no caption between them. Sound: none of its own (the clip audio plays).
graphics.avoid: Do not put a box behind it.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Article screenshot
graphics.text: Newspaper crop (90-100% width, zoomed on the headline, slight vignette) or white web page (about 64% wide, 45-85% seen). Lands by hard cut, 1-frame ghost or 5-frame crossfade, then drifts slowly upward (about 10-20% of frame height in 1-2 s, then eases to a hold); one case had a ~3 degree tilt. Motion = highlighter: orange or yellow band with rounded, dark-edged ends wipes LEFT TO RIGHT behind the key line, 10-15 frames per line (28 for a slow full line), starting about 1.1-3 s in (late on web pages, about 2.5 s). Out: crossfade into footage, often with a cyan tint and an 'ACTUAL FOOTAGE' label. Sound: none at the cut; a low boom (+24 dB) may sit on the highlight start.
graphics.avoid: Do not show it small or without a highlight. Do not freeze it fully still. Owner v4: do not use in Abyssal edits (no website/headline graphics).
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document

graphics.title: Social/web screenshot
graphics.text: Reddit/forum crop full frame (white page, slow push-in ~10% over 2 s); web page shown full frame over dark footage; phone lock-screen alerts (white mono on black, digits turn red at +2-3 s); chat bubble ~22% w x 100% h centred on a giant blurred copy of its own text; channel card lower third (~55%, rounded dark box, drop shadow) slides up in 5 frames with the name typed on; page tilted ~5 degrees over colour. Reddit handles were left readable in one clip; blur or black-box private people's names. Static hold; motion = amber marker highlight with a thin black underline that sweeps left to right, line by line (seen mid-sweep at ~3 s and done on two lines by 5 s; ~25-30 frames per sweep from +1.0-2.6 s), typing or colour change. In: 2-frame white flash, 5-frame dissolve, or glitch + hard cut. Sound: low hit +8 to +12 dB at +0.1 s (3 of 6).
graphics.avoid: Do not show real usernames of private people. Owner v4: do not use in Abyssal edits (no website/headline graphics).
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document

graphics.title: Quote card
graphics.text: Three looks: (a) white box (~79% wide, x 10-89%, y 36-65%, slight paper texture), black typewriter text, centred, over bright blurred footage; an orange highlight sweeps the first words; (b) small white typewriter text with no box straight on a heavily darkened shot (about 85% dimmed), lines 80-95% wide, centred, a new line added every ~2 s (y 35%, 58%, 68%); (c) white pixel caps, left-aligned. Text types ~1 character per frame (a long quote ~3.5 s) or blurred glitch characters resolve left to right over ~2 s. Often over red/yellow/blue posterised footage. Ends on a cut to black or the next shot. Sound: none (4 of 6).
graphics.use: A person's words from a post or video.
graphics.avoid: Do not use over clean footage.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Red number
graphics.text: Bold red typewriter/mono numbers ('65,000 texts', '£450', '$600,000'), centred at y 46-58%, no backing, often on a blurred phone or photo. Width follows the text: about 14% for a short figure, about 47% for a number plus a word. Fade/flicker in over 2 frames, ~2-5 s after the cut, held to the end of the shot. Sound: low boom (+17 to +20 dB) at the cut (3 of 6).
graphics.avoid: Do not use for dates.
graphics.situation: Stress a number, fact or outcome

graphics.title: Red marker
graphics.text: Highlight bar: red/crimson band (25-67% width, about 7% tall, rounded inked edges, dark text stays readable through it) wipes LEFT TO RIGHT behind the line, ~0.7 s per line, from 0.1-3.0 s after the cut; line by line on phone alerts. Arrow: flat/glossy red, 4-17% width, pops in over 1-3 frames 1.5-3.7 s after the cut (clip 2 shows it at about 5 s), pointing at the subject. Hand-drawn variant: red pen loop plus arrowhead, about 40% wide, line 2-3% of frame, on a zoomed shot. Circle: thin ring, no fill, white or red, sized to the subject (5-25%; as small as 5% on CCTV), present from the cut, may drift to follow a moving subject. Spotlight: soft disc 35-45% width, rest dimmed to near-black, 1-frame flash at the cut. All hold to the shot end. Sound: high-band riser +17 to +30 dB into highlights, arrows and spotlights; circles silent.
graphics.avoid: Do not use more than one marker at a time. Do not draw a large ring on a small subject.

graphics.title: Photo ID card
graphics.text: One still at a time, centred: card ~36-38% of frame width x ~73-78% tall, thin white border (~1%), a hard black shadow on the right edge (~2%), over a giant blurred copy of the same image. The name sits under it in tiny white pixel caps (~3.5% tall, ~32% wide) or in an orange tag as wide as the card. Static hold ~1-3 s, then a hard cut to the next person's card. For two or more people, show their cards one after another, not side by side.
graphics.use: Two or more people in one case.
graphics.avoid: Do not tilt it or add 3D. Do not put several photos side by side.

graphics.title: Inset on blur
graphics.text: Portrait (3:4-4:5) photo or clip centred, over an enlarged, blurred, darkened copy of itself (colour tint such as pink or B&W grain option). Vertical phone clip: ~48% width (x 26-74%), full height, hard edges. Photo: 33-48% width. Framed-photo variant: ~37% w x 80% h with a hard drop shadow ~5 px right/down. Collage variant: a portrait (~28% w, y 14-80%) beside two clips in one strip (x 14-86%). Hard cut or 3-4 frame dissolve in; inset static, background drifts slowly. Typed date: white pixel caps, ~85% width, y 49%, typed one letter per frame with a red block cursor, held ~1.5 s then gone. Name tag: black typewriter on an orange box with thin outline, ~49% width, bottom centre (y 88-95%), shown after the date. Sound: optional high riser (+16 dB).
graphics.use: Single photo of a person or object.
graphics.avoid: Do not leave black bars. Owner v4: no crossfades or dissolves; enter by hard cut or dip to black.

graphics.title: Vertical clip fill
graphics.text: 9:16 clip centred at 25-40% width and 70-100% of frame height, sides filled with an enlarged blurred copy (often near black with soft colour blobs; side flare/colour drift allowed). Hard cut, a 1-frame datamosh glitch, or a 3-frame dissolve; centre static or grows about 1% over 2 s. Sound: optional mild riser or low hit.
graphics.avoid: Do not stretch to fill. Owner v4: no crossfades or dissolves; enter by hard cut or dip to black.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)

graphics.title: Split panels
graphics.text: Hard 50/50 vertical split (seam at x 50%), no border or gap, two tall crops (each about 50% x 100%, near square). Hard cut or glitch in, static 3+ s. One side may grade to deep red (crimson, crushed blacks) over about 0.8-1 s while the other goes black and white and high contrast. An orange name strip may show for the first second. Out: red/blue block glitch tear for 2-3 frames, then hard cut. Sound: none (5 of 6).
graphics.avoid: Do not use more than 3 panels. Do not add a border between panels.

graphics.title: CRT window
graphics.text: Page shown inside a glowing blue CRT or old-Mac window with bloom.
graphics.avoid: Do not use for news articles.
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document

graphics.title: Posterise glitch frame
graphics.text: Full-frame quantise to 3-6 flat colours (black, white, cyan, royal blue with a little green; or red/yellow/black/white/cyan), soft blobby edges, no grain, footage keeps moving. A slice/tile glitch leads in over 2-4 frames. It can hold 2+ s to the shot end, also as a backdrop behind a photo card, or flash as a 2-frame threshold glitch. Sound: high riser +17 to +30 dB when it starts on the cut. Owner 2026-11-12: do NOT use on clips (no inverted/mirrored/posterised looks anywhere); ref note only.
graphics.avoid: Never on clips, intro included.
graphics.situation: Something breaks, goes wrong or feels uncanny

graphics.title: Time jump
graphics.text: Mono caption ('2 Years') or a blue 'UPLOADING ..' bar with a % counter that climbs ~1% per frame.
graphics.avoid: Do not use a clock animation.

graphics.title: 911 audio meter
graphics.text: Audio level meter graphic with captions while a call plays.
graphics.avoid: Do not leave a still frame without motion.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Host cutaway badge
graphics.text: Small subscribe/channel badge bottom-left on host cutaways.
graphics.avoid: Do not cover the host's face.

graphics.title: End card
graphics.text: 'THANKS FOR WATCHING' in white pixel mono caps, about 48% width (x 26-74%), text band y 10.5-15.5% from the top, centred, on pure black (faint TV static at most). Before it: a 3-frame colour glitch of the last shot. In: hard cut with grey text for 1-2 frames, white by +0.2 s (or 3-5 frame fade from black). One 1-frame scrambled-text glitch at ~+1.4 s. Otherwise the text sits perfectly still. Hold 4+ s (6-7 s seen). Sound: drop to near silence at the cut, a +17 dB static burst on the glitch frame.
graphics.avoid: Do not add end-screen clutter over it.

graphics.title: Patreon Level 8 card
graphics.text: Dark grey cracked-stone frame with vignette. Bold rounded white sans with soft white glow and black drop shadow, all centred: 'Level 8 of every episode is now available' (2-98% width, y 44%), 'on' + a red box with an orange-yellow glowing edge holding the Patreon URL (box x 18-92%, y 54%), small '(link in the description)' (about 30% wide, y 85%). In: a 3D raven (or cyan-edged shark silhouette) flies across the red 'LEVEL 8' iceberg and wipes it off in 4-6 frames. Hold ~2-3 s. Out: fade down to black over about 1 s (8 frames at the end), 1 pink/blue glitch frame, hard cut. Sound: low hit +8 to +11 dB on the wipe, not on the cut.
graphics.use: End block, right after the red 'LEVEL 8' teaser iceberg.
graphics.avoid: Do not use a thin font or drop the glow; keep the URL box red.

graphics.title: Glitch cut
graphics.text: 2-3 frames (0.2-0.3 s) between two shots: RGB-split scanline tear, blocky pixel corruption of the whole frame (cells ~4% wide, white/blue/black with magenta and green specks), black frame with white horizontal bars, colour smear, or a 1-frame blown white/cyan flash. Starts at the last frame of the old shot; hard cut to the new shot at +0.1-0.2 s, no fade. 3-89 per video (median ~42). Sound: high-band static spike +24 to +35 dB on the cut (5 of 6).
graphics.use: Entry and title exits, shock cuts, into the end card.
graphics.avoid: Do not fade or dissolve. Do not hold the glitch past 3 frames.

graphics_summary: Small fixed kit, all mono, dark and VHS-textured. Things move in only 4 ways: typing (1-1.5 characters per frame), left-to-right highlight wipes, 2-3 frame glitch cuts, and fades through black. Stills hold still. Sound sits on events: glitch ticks on cuts, low booms on dates, numbers and wipes, risers into highlights.

learnings.text: The warning card is small and grey, and the static sits at both top and bottom edges, not only the lower half.
learnings.note: Learn from clips (g-40215406): Black frame with grey-white pixel caps, no box, and white dash-noise bands plus grey smear bands scrolling at top and bottom. WARNING: appears alone first, then FLASH IMAGE SHOWN; in one clip the card is followed by a grey serif 'Abyssal Detective Present' over smeared colour glitch footage.

learnings.text: The title text fades from white to cyan across the line, and the entry ends by going to black.
learnings.note: Learn from clips (g-7daa450f): Black first, then iceberg close-up (pale ice, dark teal sky) with small white spaced sans caps, 1-2 lines, a white-to-cyan gradient with glow, centred at y 42-52%. Text scrambles in, holds still, and the shot goes back to black at the end.

learnings.text: The typewriter name tag is wider (about 48%) and sits near the bottom (y 90%); the sans tag sits right of centre.
learnings.note: Learn from clips (g-e64eef5e): Two looks seen. Clip 1: small bold sans caps name with a thin rule and a small mixed-case role line, lower right of centre. Clip 2: pale pink-white typewriter name, bottom centre, about half the frame wide. Both leave with a glitch or hard cut.

learnings.text: The red phrase is bold sans inside a white headline on a black band (4-96% wide, y 40-60%); the lower-left red caps variant scrambles in and fades out within about 1.5 s.
learnings.note: Learn from clips (g-83c6a79d): Clip 1 is a news headline card: small grey source tag, white bold sans on a dark band ~92% wide with the key phrase in red. Clip 2 shows glitch-scrambled bold red caps at lower left over a face; no asterisk censoring is visible in either clip.

learnings.text: On a very dark shot the text needs no box; on bright footage it sits in a white box with a blur-to-sharp reveal.
learnings.note: Learn from clips (g-89184213): Clip 1: white typewriter text straight on a heavily darkened interview shot, no box, lines added one after another. Clip 2: white paper box with black typewriter text, characters sharpening from blur left to right.

learnings.text: The inset can be full height at ~48% width for vertical video, or a multi-photo strip; the date types in pixel caps with a red block cursor and the name tag is a black typewriter on an orange box.
learnings.note: Learn from clips (g-c8aed192): Clip 1: a vertical phone clip (~48% wide, full height) over its darkened blurred copy, hard cut, no text. Clip 2: a three-panel photo collage (portrait ~28% wide plus two clips) over a pink blurred copy, with a typed white pixel date with a red cursor block, then an orange name tag.

learnings.text: Highlights are an amber marker band or a yellow double-arrow underline that moves one line at a time with the voice, not a pop-on box.
learnings.note: Learn from clips (r-ddfd118d): Clip 1: an amber marker band with a thin dark lower edge covers the Reddit comment text line by line (one line at 3 s, two lines by 5 s). Clip 2: a yellow arrow-ended underline stroke steps down the message line by line, in time with the spoken caption words.

learnings.text: The title is sized to the picture under it: about 52% of frame width over full-frame footage, about 37% (the width of the clip) over a vertical clip.
learnings.note: Learn from clips (g-2f68a909): Two-line white pixel caps 'ABYSSAL DETECTIVE / PRESENTS' with scanline fringe over a glitched face with a red waveform band, and over a vertical explosion clip with blurred sides. Text is garbled at the start, clear mid-clip, gone by 4.5 s in clip 1.

learnings.text: A credit can also be a dark-navy box with white bold sans caps, about 32% wide, top-right. It may be burned into the source clip.
learnings.note: Learn from clips (g-2bd23af5): Clip 1 shows a small dark-navy box with white bold sans caps 'AARON RIGSBY / LSM' at top-right on drone wreckage, static while the shot zooms, gone when the shot changes. Clip 2 shows a pixel-font date stamp 'AUGUST 15, 2026', not a credit.
